skill.name: documentation
skill.description: Creates structured Markdown documents for plans, proposals, notes, guides, specifications, designs, READMEs, and other long-form content.
skill.summary: Creates clear Markdown documents with structured sections, concise prose, suitable tone, and optional Mermaid diagrams.
skill.author: BfdCampos

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline-code formatting and ordinary writing guidance. SKILL.md contains no shell execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, network access, or other harmful intent.

content.value_statement: Unstructured documents make important information difficult to find and use. This skill organizes Markdown content with clear sections, concise prose, suitable formatting, and optional diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Creates long-form content as Markdown files with sensible names.
Structures documents with headers, short paragraphs, lists, bullets, and tables.
Formats commands and configuration examples in code blocks.
Adjusts tone for technical documents, proposals, brainstorms, and plans.
Uses Mermaid diagrams when architecture, flows, or relationships need visualization.
Uses emojis selectively when they improve navigation in informal documents.
limitations: It does not verify the factual accuracy of source material.
It does not provide domain-specific templates or mandatory compliance structures.
Diagram creation depends on a separately available Mermaid skill.
It does not define document versioning, review, approval, or publishing workflows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Documentation
use_cases.description: Create readable READMEs, setup guides, and technical notes for software projects.

use_cases.title: Structure Plans and Proposals
use_cases.description: Turn objectives, constraints, and decisions into actionable plans or persuasive proposals.

use_cases.title: Develop Technical Guides
use_cases.description: Organize complex source material into clear guides, specifications, and design documents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Topic Note
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Markdown note about [topic]. Use clear headers, short paragraphs, and bullet points. Save it with a sensible filename.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Project README
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a README for [project]. Include an overview, installation, usage, configuration, and limitations. Format commands and configurations in code blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Decision Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a proposal for [decision]. Explain the problem, options, recommendation, benefits, risks, and next steps. Keep the argument persuasive and honest.

prompt_templates.title: Develop an Architecture Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture specification for [system] using [source material]. Cover context, components, data flows, decisions, risks, and unresolved questions. Add a Mermaid diagram when relationships need visualization. Distinguish confirmed facts from assumptions.

output_examples.input: Create a README for a command-line backup tool.
output: Project overview explaining the backup tool and its purpose.
Installation and usage sections with clearly formatted commands.

output_examples.input: Turn meeting notes into an implementation plan.
output_examples.output: A structured plan containing objectives, scope, concrete tasks, dependencies, risks, owners, and next steps.

output_examples.input: Document the data flow between an application and its services.
output_examples.output: An architecture document describing components, interfaces, data movement, decisions, and a Mermaid flow diagram.

best_practices: Provide the audience, purpose, source material, and required sections before generation.
Review factual claims, commands, and configuration details before publishing.
Use diagrams only when they clarify relationships that prose cannot explain efficiently.
anti_patterns: Do not request a document without supplying available facts or context.
Do not use excessive formatting, emojis, or diagrams in formal technical documents.
Do not treat generated content as verified evidence or approved policy.

faq.question: Which document format does this skill use?
faq.answer: It focuses on Markdown files for plans, proposals, notes, guides, specifications, designs, and READMEs.

faq.question: Can it write technical and nontechnical documents?
faq.answer: Yes. It adjusts tone and structure to match technical documents, proposals, brainstorms, and plans.

faq.question: Can it create diagrams?
faq.answer: It recommends Mermaid diagrams and can use a separately available Mermaid skill.

faq.question: How does it make documents readable?
faq.answer: It uses headers, short paragraphs, lists, tables, code blocks, and selective emphasis.

faq.question: Does it verify facts and commands?
faq.answer: No. Users must review factual claims, commands, and configuration details before publishing.

faq.question: Where does it place generated content?
faq.answer: It writes long-form content to a sensibly named Markdown file and reports the file location.
